text:
sara: getting pages for a sudden spike of HF 429s — model pulls failing since ~10:12 UTC. lots of our cold-starts stuck in `fetch_artifact` step. console shows upstream returned 429 rate_limit in the logs. anyone else seeing this?

matt: yup seeing the same. error snippet from host: `GET https://huggingface.co/api/models/… 429 Too Many Requests`. High error rate on model load path. Paging oncall. :rotating_light:

incident-bot: Incident created (P1) — title autogenerated: 'third_party_model_fetch_errors' — paging matt (oncall). Link: https://redwood.inc/incident/1835000000

matt: I'm on it. immediately flipping canary -> cached-model fallback for the slow-path. Executing rollout script now.

sara: customer-visible: several prod routes returning 503s during cold start. observed 120 failing requests in last 5m, 3 customers flagged with >30% errors.

matt: mitigation 1) enable cache-only model serving for recent model versions (no remote fetch) 2) increase fetch retry backoff (exponential with jitter) 3) route new requests to warm pool where model already loaded. Doing 1+2 now.

emily: copying the small config we use for regional caching: ```
model_fetch:
  strategy: cache-first
  max_retries: 2
  backoff_ms: 500, 1500, 4000
  retry_on: [429, 502, 503]
```

matt: pushed change to prod: `cache-first` enabled for default model route. patch id `deploy/infra/1835-cache-fallback`. Rollout to 50% -> watching.

ops-bot: deploy started: deploy/infra/1835-cache-fallback by matt — staging -> prod (canary 50%). CI: passed.

dennis: have we checked our HF token quotas? could be org-level throttling on HF side.

matt: good call. I grabbed token headers — HF returns `x-ratelimit-limit` headers but they're inconsistent. Opening HF status: https://status.huggingface.co — shows "degraded performance" in assets CDN.

sara: external issue then. we should inform support and cut a status page message. I'll draft a short note for status.redwood: affected model fetches causing elevated cold-start failures; mitigation in place (cache fallback).

emily: also started warmup jobs for top 5 heavy models from S3 cached blobs to avoid further cold starts. command: ```for m in $(cat top_models.txt); do trigger_warmup $m; done```

matt: after enabling cache-first, error rate dropped from ~35% to ~6% on affected routes. latency on first token still higher for non-cached but acceptable. Monitoring for any regression.

incident-bot: Pager escalation timer extended for 30m (mitigation active).

dennis: matching customers impacted: acct-42 (internal sandbox) acct-77 (heavy inference), acct-190 (batch pipeline). I've DM'd AE to notify the three.

sara: numbers update: 10m window now: total fetch failures 230 -> fell to 40 after fallback. No new customer tickets yet but telemetry might lag.

matt: temp ACL to reduce concurrent HF fetches per region: `max_concurrent_hf_fetches: 8` set. This will queue extra fetches into our warmup queue instead of hammering HF.

emily: added a short-circuit in runtime so that if HF returns 429 and there's a recent local tarball, we use it even if model version slightly mismatches within tolerated patch. Logged as `fetch_fallback_local`.

sara: kicked off contact with HF via workspace support ticket #HF-9892: shared request ids and timestamps. They acknowledged limited CDN capacity and are throttling artifact downloads.

matt: prepping handoff to emily in 30m for night coverage. Emily, main things to watch: errors on /model/load, errors/sec, warmup queue depth, and whether HF recovers. escalation path if cache fallback fails: 1) enable smaller model variant fallback (quantized) 2) degrade non-critical customers to best-effort mode 3) engage infra lead for emergency egress bursts.

emily: ack. I'll take over at 10:50 UTC. Also creating a short runbook note in incidents-runbooks: "hf-asset-throttle" with steps we followed.

ops-bot: note added to incident: runs /incidents/1835000000/notes (author: emily)

matt: quick diagnostic logs attached: ```
[10:14:05] fetch_artifact model-x v2 -> 429 from hf, request_id=abc123
[10:14:06] queued to warmup queue
[10:15:12] fallback to local tarball ok
```

dennis: can we estimate customer-impact minutes to include in post-incident report? sara, any calc?

sara: rough calc: 3 customers * avg 5 RPS * 8 minutes peak = ~720 impacted requests (some retries). I'll refine with logs.

incident-bot: postmortem reminder scheduled. Owner: matt. Deadline: 72h.

emily: handover note: cache-fallback active, warmup jobs running, HF support ticket open, watchlist: acct-77 telemetry. I'll escalate to infra if fallback errors exceed 10% for 20m.

matt: thanks team. heading to brief with sales for the customers. leaving the thread to emily.

emily: taking over. tagging #incidents-ops for visibility. updating status.redwood to reflect mitigation and ongoing HF degraded performance.

sara: adding this to customer-impact spreadsheet and pinging CS. also adding link to HF ticket in incident doc.

incident-bot: incident status: Mitigated -> monitoring. Time to mitigate: ~8 minutes from page.

emily: closing handoff. will update thread when HF fully recovers or if rollback needed. :white_check_mark:
